Make the root's exchange meet these, counted by the bot from what it played

What I see: chunky blue/yellow and red box robots on a sunlit tiled pitch, a ringed blue robot walking at a red one, sliding, the red one flipping into the air, then a shot with a white burst at the goal. Worst for a newcomer: the exchange and the ball keep getting hidden. The captain's own body covers the ball and carrier (images 1 and 9), the camera looks through a goal net at the captain (images 5 and 13), bursts swallow the bodies with no ball visible (images 6 and 14), and the overview misses the play (images 7 and 15). Checklist items failing in these frames: 4, 5, 11, 24, 26, 28.

slop camera_hides_exchange (images 1, 9, 6, 14): on approach the captain stands directly between the lens and the ball and the Docker's legs. Raise the play camera or offset it sideways so ball, carrier and captain's feet stay separate. The kept 'Behind Your Bot' choice asks to see two teammates ahead; images 1, 2, 9 and 10 show none.

slop camera_behind_scenery (images 5 and 13): near the captain's own goal the camera sits behind the net, so bars cross the captain, two other robots and the ball for the whole strip. The kicked ball then goes behind the barrier blocks to the right of the goal and is lost (image 5, tiles 7-12). It reads as leaving the pitch or passing through the wall.

claim contradicted: one_timer at frame 4687 (images 7 and 15). The overview strip shows only the red keeper at the far goal on an empty pitch, plus a tiny white puff at left. No wind-up, hit or reaction is on it. The play-camera strip of the same frames (image 5) shows the captain knocking a ball that was already beside it, with no incoming pass visible, so no one-timer reads there either.

No hit-stop is visible: in the contact strips (images 2, 4, 5, 6) no two or three tiles hold both bodies still. The slide (image 1) goes from upright to flat within about 5 frames with no readable wind-up. From behind, the sliding captain looks like a blue cross lying down. Add a crouch or lean anticipation, a side-readable slide pose, and a short hold on both bodies at contact.

The best moment is the tackle (image 1, last tile; image 3, last tile): the Docker is clearly airborne and tumbling with a burst and ring. The strip ends on that frame, and the loose ball, pickup and wind-up between frames 59 and 124 are not filmed. In image 2 the red victim is upright again by about the third tile, before the shot arrives, so 'score while it clambers' barely reads. Lengthen the get-up and keep it in frame.

The goal does not read as a goal (images 2, 4, 10, 12): a burst appears at the mouth, but the keeper shows no clear dive or beaten reaction and the score stays 3:2 through frame 146. In the play view the scoreboard is cut off at the top at that very moment (images 2, 10, 6, 14), so the change could not be seen there. Keep the score in frame or add a screen score pop (items 24, 26).

Effects hide play and appear from nowhere: large glowing orbs cover the blue mate and red robot (images 6 and 14, tiles 7-12), and no ball can be found anywhere in that strip. White bursts also appear on open pitch with no robot or ball at them (images 4, 8, 12, 15, 16). Shrink and shorten the bursts, anchor each to its cause, and never draw them over the ball.

Items 4 and 5: no frame, including the first 60 (images 1 and 9), shows a rule, goal or 'Space slides' hint. Nothing marks which goal is yours, where an off-screen ball or mate is, or what the threat is. The scoreboard digits are yellow and cyan while the teams are blue/yellow and red, so a newcomer cannot tell who has 3.

Item 11: no rival attack or readable tell appears in any strip, so the claim tells 3 / tell_min_f 20 is unverified on film. The red carrier in images 1 and 3 simply holds position while the captain closes and slides, with no hop, pass or evasion visible.

claim contradicted: verbs_used 5. The strips (images 1-8) show running, a slide and kicks or shots only; no hop and no clearly readable pass appears. The clip moments skittle_goal and hop_cross_finish are not on film.

Ball and size: the yellow ball with a red ring is close in colour to the captain's yellow torso and feet and to the red target ring, and disappears against them (images 1, 9). In the overview, robots and ball are specks on a large empty pitch (images 3, 4, 11, 12). Give the ball a distinct colour or marker.

In images 6 and 14 the blue mate and a red robot press into one clump at the goalmouth under the effects, and a downed red robot lies in the same pose through all 12 tiles with a smoke trail. Keep bodies separated and show the get-up progressing.

Mood (images 1-16): the toon ink style and palette hang together, but this reads as a sunny or sunset meadow stadium with pine forest and mountains. There is no night, scrapyard cage or visible tin-can crowd; the stands are empty seats. This belongs to the look package and comes after the camera and ball fixes.

Against the house game (image 17): this build shows a victim's flight more plainly than the house strip, which is a crowded stick scrum. It falls short in keeping the object of play visible (ball lost in images 5 and 6) and shows no hit-stop.
